signals.source: rotating-expert-review (dispatcher Tier-1d 2026-09-21 reality-web currency-format crash sink)
evidence: `new Intl.NumberFormat(locale, { style: 'currency', currency }).format(v)` throws `RangeError: Invalid currency code` whenever `currency` is a non-empty but malformed ISO-4217 code (wrong length or non-alpha: '', already handled elsewhere, but also 'US', 'EURO', '€', '12', 'eu'). The `currency` value flows straight from listing/API data (`listing.currency`) with no validation and no try/catch, so a single malformed listing crashes the React render subtree.

frontend/apps/reality-web/src/components/listings/ListingCard.tsx:106 — `{formatPrice(listing.price, locale, { currency: listing.currency })}` OVERRIDES format.ts's safe `currency:'EUR'` default (lib/format.ts:48-59 has no try/catch) with the raw per-listing currency. ListingCard renders in the PUBLIC search/results grid, so one bad listing throws and takes down the whole grid page.

frontend/apps/reality-web/src/components/comparison/ComparisonView.tsx:37-41 — formatPrice useMemo does `currency = listing?.currency ?? 'EUR'` then `Intl.NumberFormat({style:'currency',currency}).format(Number(value))` with NO try/catch. The `??` only guards null/undefined, not a malformed non-empty string; a listing loaded via the shared-comparison URL handler (?ids=... -> API fetch) with a bad currency crashes the comparison view. (`Number(value)` on a non-numeric price additionally renders the literal 'NaN', a lesser cosmetic bug.)
frontend/apps/reality-web/src/components/agency/AgencyListings.tsx:372-377 — same unguarded `Intl.NumberFormat({style:'currency',currency})` on the agency listings table.

Reference for the correct fix already exists in-repo: frontend/apps/reality-web/src/app/[locale]/realtor/listings/page.tsx:16-22 wraps the identical call in try/catch and falls back to `${value} ${currency}`. Confidence MEDIUM (static-only): the throw semantics of Intl.NumberFormat on a bad currency code and the absence of any guard at these sites are confirmed by direct read; NOT confirmed is whether reality-server guarantees a valid ISO-4217 currency on every listing row (if it does, this degrades to defense-in-depth; if a legacy/imported/CSV-onboarded listing can carry a bad code, it is a live crash).

Fix (cloud-landable, frontend-only): add a shared `formatCurrency(value, locale, currency)` helper (or extend lib/format.ts formatPrice) that try/catches the currency path and falls back to a plain grouped number + code, then route ListingCard, ComparisonView and AgencyListings through it. Single-package change under frontend/apps/reality-web/src/, verifies with pnpm --filter @ppt/reality-web typecheck/test + biome; no backend/build coupling.

signals.source: rotating-expert-review (dispatcher Tier-1d 2026-09-21 reality-web SSR listing-section currency guard gap)
evidence: frontend/apps/reality-web/src/components/listings/sections/ListingHeader.tsx:6-16 and AdditionalInfo.tsx:6-16 both guard the currency path with only `if (typeof currency !== 'string' || currency.length === 0)`. That check catches empty/null but NOT a non-empty malformed code: 'US' (2 chars), 'EURO' (4 chars), '€', or digits all pass `length === 0` yet still make `new Intl.NumberFormat('en-US', { style:'currency', currency }).format(value)` throw `RangeError: Invalid currency code`. The empty-string guard gives a false sense of safety.

These two components are section renderers on the PUBLIC listing detail page (app/[locale]/listings/[slug]/page.tsx, SSR/ISR). A throw here happens during server render, so a single listing with a malformed non-empty currency yields an HTTP 500 on an SEO-indexed public URL (worse than the client-only crash in finding-1). getListing()'s parseListingDetail normalizer validates shape but does NOT normalize/validate the currency code against ISO-4217, so a bad code survives into these renderers.

Distinct from finding-1 (different files, and here a guard EXISTS but is insufficient — the fix is to widen the guard, not add one from scratch) and distinct from the SSR-hardening already credited on getListing. Confidence MEDIUM (static-only): the incomplete guard and the SSR render path are confirmed by direct read; the live-500 depends on whether a wrong-length/non-alpha currency can reach the row (see finding-1 caveat).

Fix (cloud-landable, frontend-only): replace the `length === 0` check with a try/catch around the currency Intl.NumberFormat (mirroring app/[locale]/realtor/listings/page.tsx:16-22) or a strict `/^[A-Za-z]{3}$/` validation before formatting, in both section files. Single-package reality-web edit, verifies with typecheck/test + biome.
